# Draft:Daily Item Replacements that are Eco-Friendly & Help Reduce Global Warming

Introduction
Climate Change & Global Warming will eventually damage our planet forever, but humans are working together to end this global crisis. The best way you can help others solve this problem is by making these replacements in daily items. From cups & plates to the types of lightbulbs you use. Let’s start the list.
AI - Artificial Intelligence
AI has skyrocketed in popularity in the United States, especially for ChatGPT.
What’s wrong with these types of popular AI’s?
They use huge amounts of water to cool down their systems.
Such as ChatGPT: About 36.19 million gallons of water per day.
Replacement AI to Use: Google Gemini AI
Gemini: About 171,711 gallons of water per day.
Gemini is a better alternative, due to using way less water than other AIs.
Tip:
Try to use AI very frequently; instead, use browser sites (Ex, Google, Bing, etc.)
Water Bottles
Replacements:
Stainless Steel Water Bottles
Water Bottles made from Recycled Materials/Recycled Plastic
Preferably, Any Reusable Water Bottles
Thermal/Thermos Water Bottles
Tip:
Try to use one Water Bottle per day, with refills.
Cups
Preferably, Any Reusable Water Bottles
Stainless Steel Cups
Glass Cups
Ceramic Cups
Wooden Cups
Tip:
Try to use one Cup for drinks per day, limiting the amount of water needed to wash it, also helping with less frequent dishwasher loads, saving gallons of water.
Silverware
Reuseable Silverware
Stainless Steel Silverware
Bamboo Silverware
Birch Wood Silverware
Tip:
Try to limit the amount of silverware you use per day to reduce dishwasher loads and save water.
Plates & Bowls
Reusable Plates & Bowls
Ceramic Plates & Bowls
Glass Plates & Bowls
Porcelain Plates & Bowls
Stoneware Plates & Bowls
Stainless Steel Plates & Bowls
Wooden Plates & Bowls
Tip:
Try to only use about 3-4 plates/bowls per day, one plate/bowl per meal per person.
Soaps & Dishsoap
Solid Bars of Soap/Dishsoap
Dishsoap Powder Refill Tablets
Natural Soaps/Dishsoaps
Tip:
Try to limit the amount of soap/dish soap to save money and not waste it.
Drying Dishes/Silverware
Drying Racks
Drying Mat
Tip:
Letting your dishes/silverware air dry is the best thing you can do for the environment in your kitchen, even though you may already do it.
Towels
Reuseable Towels
Organic Cotton Towels
Hemp Towels
Linen Towels
Bamboo Towels
Recycled Fiber Towels
Tip:
If you want to make eco-friendly decisions in your household, make sure to almost ALWAYS avoid paper towels; having reusable towels is a key factor for being eco-friendly. Using more reusable towels saves you money as well, including many other reusable items.
Tissues
Handkerchiefs
100% Recycled Tissues
Tips:
Tissues are also recommended to avoid, but not as harmful as paper towels.
Handkerchiefs are amazing options for tissue replacements, due to being reusable, foldable, made with natural cotton, and washable.
Napkins
Reusable Cloth Napkins
Organic Cotton
Linen
Hemp
Sugarcane Fiber
Bamboo Fiber
100% Recycled Napkins
Tip:
Napkins also fall into the category of being harmful, being as harmful as tissues, but there are a lot more options for napkins, such as reusable napkins, usually seen at restaurants.
Shopping Bags
Reusable Bags
Cotton (Heavy Duty)
Recyclable Bags
Compostable Plastic Bags
Tip:
Having reusable bags in your trunk for groceries is one of the most eco-friendly things you can do in your everyday life. The amount of plastic bags littered on the ground in the world is a big problem, and doing this helps solve the problem, one person at a time.
Traveling
Bikes, Electric Bikes
Walking
Running
Electric vehicles
Electric Scooters
Tips:
Try to walk to more local places, rather than driving each time, unless you have an electric car that doesn’t release harmful greenhouse gases.
Try to use cars over planes, especially for short distances, as cars release less CO2 than planes.
When booking a flight, try to go to the details section, which should have the amount of CO2 that will most likely be released into the atmosphere. Try to book the flight with the least amount of CO2 released.
Trash & Recycling
Reusable Recycling Bins
Reusable Trash Bins
Reusable & Washable Trash Bags
Tip:
Try to reduce the amount of products you use that aren’t recyclable; these types of products aren’t used for anything, while recyclable products eventually get reused and made into new products.
Mugs
Stainless Steel Mugs
Wooden Mugs
Metal Insulated Travel Mugs
Tip:
Try to limit the amount of mugs used per day, making it so there are fewer dishwasher loads, saving water.
Sponges
Compostable Sponges
Wooden Dish Brushes
Metal Scrubbers
Tip:
Try to wash your sponges every day, so they last longer and don’t decompose from the soap over time.
Straws
Reusable Straws
Metal Straws
Bamboo Straws
Wooden Straws
Silicone Straws
Tip:
Try to avoid plastic reusable straws and aim for metal or wooden straws.
Toothbrush
Electric Toothbrush
Bamboo Toothbrush
Wooden Toothbrush
Tip:
Try to use more natural material tooth brushes.
Razors
Electric Razors
Recyclable Razors
Metal Safety Razors (w/ Replaceable Blades)
Tip:
Try to stick to reusable razors, rather than disposable ones.
Dryer Sheets
Wool Dryer Balls
Recyclable Dryer Sheets
Tip:
Wool Dryer Balls are a very good replacement in your home, being reusable for years at a time.
Batteries
Rechargeable Batteries
Recyclable Batteries
Tip:
Using Rechargeable Batteries are very helpful and eco-friendly, also saving money.
Food Storage
Glass Containers
Metal Containers
Reusable Silicone Storage Bags
Tip:
Try to use more reusable containers and storage bags to be eco-friendly and save money.
Light Bulbs
LED Light Bulbs
Tip:
Replacing your traditional light bulbs with LED light bulbs improves your home in many ways. LED’s last longer, are more energy efficient, and are eco-friendly.
Overall Energy/Power
Solar Panels
Mini Wind Turbines
Tip:
Using natural resources like the sun’s light and the wind are amazing ways to get your energy and power in an eco-friendly way!
Pens/Pencils
Refillable Ink Pens
Metal Mechanical Pencils
Tip:
Try to avoid using normal wooden pencils, as they are eventually used up quickly after a short amount of time. Try reusable metal mechanicalpencils instead, which last forever with only needing to add led.
Paper/Notebooks
100% Recycled Paper
100% Recycled Paper Notebooks
Recyclable Paper/Notebooks
Tip:
Using Paper & Notebooks that are made from 100% recyclable items are great choices to be eco-friendly.
Plant Pots
Ceramic Pots
Clay Pots
Wooden Pots
Using clay pots is extremely eco-friendly, due to being a key natural resource.
Pet Toys
100% Recycled Toys
Wooden Toys
Long-Lasting Toys
Tip:
Using 100% Recycled Toys is the best way to make you and your pet eco-friendly.
Kids Toys
Wooden Toys
Metal Toys (Dull)
100% Recycled Toys
Tip:
It is preferred to use Wooden Toys, due to the selection and options to choose from. Many children’s toys that are wooden consist of Lincoln Logs, Blocks, and more! This time, your kid and you can be eco-friendly!
Hangers for Clothing
100% Recycled Hangers
Thick Metal Hangers (Not Wired)
Wooden Hangers
Tip:
Thick Metal Hangers is a great option due to its longevity and eco-friendliness.
Floss
Bamboo Floss Sticks
100% Recycled Floss Sticks
Silk Floss Sticks
Tip:
Bamboo Floss Sticks are highly recommended, beating plastic by far in eco-friendliness.
Conclusion
Overall, these 30 replacements for everyday items can make you more eco-friendly, one item at a time.
There are many other ways to help end this global crisis, including everyday decisions. Learn from my new Articles about Climate Change, Sustainability, the Environment, and more soon.
DNRClimate
Junior Sustainability Enthusiast
